title: Raftless throttler drain + sticky fairness protocol for limiter outage recovery
creator: Asha Rao
description: Implement a lightweight, non-consensus (raftless) drain and recovery mode for token/lease-based throttlers to maintain sticky fairness during limiter outages and cross-region failovers. Goal: ensure bounded customer impact during limiter restarts, network partitions, and regional circuit-breaker activations while keeping 99th percentile latency and error SLOs intact for premium tenants.
acceptance_criteria: During simulated limiter outage, tenant success rate degradation limited to <5% for premium SLA customers and <15% for best-effort customers over a 10-minute window.
Automatic sticky fairness rehydration preserves proportional share for long-running tenants after limiter restart without global consensus (no raft leader election required).
New drain protocol reduces error spikes on restart by at least 60% compared to current restart behavior in canary region tests.
Complete telemetry: per-tenant admitted/rejected counts, drift metric, sticky-score heatmap, and tracing of drain→rehydrate flow visible in Console dashboards.
Playbook documented with rollback criteria and runbook for SRE intervention.
End-to-end tests (chaos + load) pass in staging with quotas and KV cache enabled.
Rollout across a single region fleet behind feature flag with staged ramp to multi-region.
Security review completed for edge-case token persistence and KMS interactions.

comments: 2026-02-25 - Asha Rao: Initial ticket created after incident-2026-02-20 where regional limiter restart caused a tenant fairness reset and ~3x error spike for medium-tier customers. See incident notes link.

2026-02-28 - Ethan Park: Spike repro'd locally. Current restart sequence: ephemeral leases cleared -> global rebalancer recomputes shares -> bursts follow non-deterministic FIFO causing starvation. Prototype plan: avoid global rebalancer on restart; instead persist lightweight sticky markers per-tenant to inform local share rehydration.

2026-03-03 - Design review (Sofia Delgado): recommended marker format to be base64 encoded proto with version and TTL to avoid long-lived drift. Trade-off: small extra storage vs. avoidance of cross-region consensus. Approved 3-0.

2026-03-05 - Engineering sync: decided to implement two-phase drain: (1) soft-drain where we stop new heavy grants, continue serving existing leases for short grace window (configurable 5s-30s), (2) commit sticky markers for active tenants before fully draining. Rationale: reduces interruption and preserves proportionality without raft.
2026-03-07 - PR #11822 opened: initial implementation of sticky marker writer and soft-drain handshake. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11822
2026-03-08 - QA: early perf run shows 45% reduction in error spikes on single-region restart at 10k rps across 1k tenants. More tests needed for cross-region failover.

2026-03-10 - Security note (by Maya Singh): KMS calls occur on sticky marker persistence only for private deployments. For hosted, markers are sealed with platform key. Security review requested: confirm marker lifecycle and key rotation behavior. Assigned to Security team.

2026-03-12 - SRE runbook draft: added steps to force soft-drain, inspect sticky-score heatmap, and trigger manual marker rehydrate. Included alert threshold: sticky-drift > 0.25 for 3m triggers pager if customer_impact=high.
2026-03-14 - Ethan Park: added multi-region chaos matrix and scheduled chaos run for 2026-03-20. Also added dependency on ENG-24060 (KV cache bounded persistence improvements).
